manual_or_upload.label: Apple Health export
manual_or_upload.description: Export your Apple Health data from your iPhone, then upload the .zip (or the export.xml inside it) here.

acquisition_methods.label: Export from the Health app
acquisition_methods.detail: On your iPhone, open the Health app, tap your profile picture (top right), scroll down, and tap Export All Health Data. Confirm Export, then AirDrop, save, or share the resulting export.zip to a device where you can upload it here.

acquisition_methods.label: Upload the export XML if the .zip cannot be opened
acquisition_methods.detail: If the import says your export.zip cannot be opened here, unzip it on a computer (it contains apple_health_export/export.xml; on a phone set to another language the file name may be translated, for example eksport.xml) and, if that XML file is under 8 GB, upload it instead of the archive. The XML is larger than the .zip it came from, so this does not help an archive over the upload limit.

manual_or_upload.help_text: Apple Health does not expose an account API or OAuth grant. This source imports an owner-exported export.zip or export.xml produced by the iPhone Health app.
manual_or_upload.large_file_fallback: A full Health export can run to several GB for a long-lived account, and the XML inside export.zip is larger than the archive, so unzipping does not help an archive over the upload limit. An archive within the limit that cannot be opened here, such as one of 4 GB or more in the zip64 format, can be unzipped on a computer and its export XML uploaded instead, if that file is under 8 GB; the XML is read as a stream.
validation_expectations: Detected an Apple Health export (export.xml, standalone or inside export.zip)
Estimated health record and workout counts
Duplicate, empty, unsupported, or too-large file status

refresh_policy.rationale: Apple Health imports require the user to produce a new export.xml from iOS; cannot be refreshed in the background.

streams.name: activity
streams.description: Apple Health records of the types HealthKit's documentation groups under Activity, such as steps, distances, energy burned, flights climbed, exercise, move and stand time, stand hours, running, cycling, rowing and paddling metrics, workout effort, VO2 max and low cardio fitness notifications. Not incremental: every import re-sends every record in the export under a content-derived id, so a record already held is superseded rather than duplicated. Deletions and edits made in Health are not propagated: no tombstone is emitted, and an edited record arrives as a new record beside the old one.

display.label: Your activity
display.detail: Readings such as steps; walking, running, cycling, swimming, wheelchair, rowing, paddling, skating and snow-sports distances; flights climbed; active and resting energy; exercise, move and stand minutes and stand hours; running and cycling speed, power, cadence and form; workout effort; VO2 max, and notifications of low cardio fitness. Each reading carries its type, value and unit as the export states them; its start, end and creation dates; the time-zone offset where it was recorded, which shows when you were in another time zone; and whether it was typed in by hand. The names of the apps and devices that recorded it are not included, nor anything that identifies a particular device, so no reading carries the name someone gave their phone or watch; the device's maker, model, and hardware, firmware and software versions are kept, because a reader needs to know whether a measurement came from a watch or a chest strap. An identical reading recorded twice arrives once; on a very large export this stops once 400,000 different readings across all the health areas have been remembered, and the import receipt of each area affected says so. Readings are told apart by what they record and by the device's maker, model and hardware, not by which physical device made them or the firmware and software versions it ran: the same reading at the same times from two devices with the same maker, model and hardware arrives once, as do two otherwise identical readings whose device descriptions are missing or could not be read. Readings of the same thing from devices whose maker, model or hardware differ are all kept; they are not reconciled. Every import brings in everything in your export again: a reading you already have is updated rather than duplicated, and a reading you delete in Health is not removed here.

device.description: The device that recorded it, as the hardware fields of Apple's device description: manufacturer, model, hardware, firmware and software, in that order, for those present. Each is written key:value, with ", " (a comma and a space) before each key after the first, for example "manufacturer:Apple Inc., model:Watch, hardware:Watch6,2, software:9.1"; values are as the export states them and may themselves contain commas. Never the device's name or its identifiers. Null when the export states none of these fields, and also when a description is present but cannot be read unambiguously, because it is not in Apple's device-description form or one of these fields appears in it twice; the stream's receipt then lists device under fields_unavailable.

was_user_entered.description: True when the owner typed this reading in by hand rather than a sensor recording it. Extracted from the HKWasUserEntered metadata entry. This is the one metadata key worth publishing: it separates measured from asserted, which changes how a reader should weigh the value.

freshness.description: Always "snapshot". An Apple Health export is a point-in-time dump produced by hand on the device and is never live. Declared as a single-value enum because a reader should not have to handle a "live" case this source cannot produce.

exported_at.description: The export's own ExportDate, as stamped by the Health app. This is the age of the DATA. A reader must date Apple Health records by this and not by when collection ran.

start_utc_offset_minutes.description: Minutes east of UTC at the moment this was recorded. start_date is normalised to UTC, which keeps the instant exact but loses the wall clock the owner lived in. For health data that clock is often the fact itself - a sleep record at 23:00 local is not the same claim as 13:00 UTC - so the offset travels alongside rather than being discarded or guessed. Null when the export states no offset. Also null when it states one beyond 18 hours either side of UTC, which no time zone uses, and the stream's receipt then lists start_utc_offset_minutes under fields_unavailable.

streams.name: reproductive_health

It also carries the three symptoms HealthKit's documentation files under Reproduction (breast pain, pelvic pain and vaginal dryness). Deletions made in Health are not propagated: no tombstone is emitted. display.label: Your workouts

Such exports typically state no total distance or energy for a workout, so those are added up from the workout's own statistics, or from its activities' where those record a kind the workout's own lack, never from both; where each records a kind of distance the other lacks, the total is left empty and the import receipt says so. streams.name: coverage_diagnostics
streams.description: One receipt per requested data stream per import, saying what was covered and why it ends where it does. Like any stream, it honours a resource list: a request for specific receipt ids receives only those.

display.label: What was imported
display.detail: A short receipt for each kind of data in each import: whether everything in your export was read, how many records arrived and the earliest and latest dates among them, how many duplicates were discarded, how many entries could not be read or were of a kind this version does not recognise, the names of any fields left empty, and the date your export was taken. The receipts alone therefore show, for each kind of data, whether you have any, how many, and over what dates: for example, whether your export holds reproductive-health records, how many, and from when to when.

stream.description: The data stream this record accounts for: one of the health-area streams, or workouts.

status.description: Whether the covered window matches the requested window. A stream with records is also 'partial', whatever its window, when rows may be missing (collection_interrupted, records_unreadable) or a newer .zip could not be opened (newer_upload_too_large). 'empty' is an ordinary outcome, not a failure. Under a resource list, a record requested by id that cannot be read is not reported on the receipt, since an unreadable row has no id to match against the request; 'complete' and covered_in_full then speak only for the rows that could be read, so a reader that asked for specific ids should check that each one arrived.

reason.description: Why the covered window ends where it does. Always present, including on success, so a reader branches on the value and never on the field being absent. Each value implies a different next action for the owner and has a reason_display_messages entry. newer_upload_too_large replaces covered_in_full and nothing_in_range on the receipts of an import that read an export beside a newer .zip it could not open, for its size or the number of files it holds, since the export inside that .zip may supersede what was read; a receipt with any other reason keeps that reason.

record_count.description: Records emitted for this stream in this import.

duplicates_discarded.description: Records dropped because a record with the same identity had already been seen in this import: for a health record, the same type, device manufacturer, model and hardware, unit, dates, offset, creation stamp, reading, and whether it was typed in or sensed; for a workout, the same type, device manufacturer, model and hardware, dates, offset and duration, whatever distance and energy each states. A device's firmware and software are published but not compared, and a device description that is missing or could not be read is compared as none. Records whose device manufacturer, model or hardware differ are not reconciled and are not counted here. Two devices with the same manufacturer, model and hardware cannot be told apart, so an identical record from each, at identical times, is counted here. Suppression remembers up to 400,000 distinct identities across all the health-area streams together, and up to 100,000 workouts. A stream that meets a new identity after its budget is spent says so: its count is a floor from there, and duplicates_discarded appears under its fields_unavailable. Published because once source names are excluded a reader cannot audit any dropping from the records themselves, and a silent discard is indistinguishable from a reading that never existed.

records_skipped_unreadable.description: Rows that could not be parsed, or that the schema rejected, and were skipped. These fail identically on every retry; re-importing will not recover them. Unreadable rows are not counted when the stream was asked for specific record ids, since a row that could not be read has no id to match one against; a requested row the schema rejected is. Rows outside the requested window are not counted.

records_type_unrecognized.description: Records delivered on this stream whose type this version does not assign to any health area, for example one Apple added to HealthKit after this version was written. Such records are delivered on the other stream rather than dropped, so only the other stream's receipt can count any; grouping that stream by type shows which they are. Records outside the requested window or not asked for are not counted.

fields_unavailable.description: Fields the schema declares that were left empty, or cut short, on at least one record this import delivered for the stream, so a column of nulls is never mistaken for a column of absent readings; exported_at is listed whenever the export states no ExportDate. Records outside the requested window, not asked for, discarded as duplicates or rejected as unreadable do not contribute. One entry names a field of this receipt instead: duplicates_discarded, listed once the stream's identity budget is spent, after which that count is a floor. Empty when nothing was left out.

window_covered_from.description: Null when nothing was covered. A reader must render this window rather than the requested one.

freshness.description: Always "snapshot". An Apple Health export is a point-in-time dump produced by hand on the device and is never live. Declared as a single-value enum because a reader should not have to handle a "live" case this source cannot produce.

exported_at.description: The export's own ExportDate. The age of the data.

reason_display_messages.covered_in_full: Everything of this kind in your export for this period was imported.
reason_display_messages.nothing_in_range: Your export had no data of this kind matching this request. That's not a problem - there was simply nothing to read.
reason_display_messages.awaiting_upload: Nothing to read yet. On your iPhone open Health, tap your picture, and choose Export All Health Data. Upload the export.zip here when it's ready.
reason_display_messages.source_unreadable: That file isn't an Apple Health export we can read. It should be the export.zip your iPhone produced, or the export.xml from inside it.
reason_display_messages.export_extraction_failed: We couldn't read your export, so nothing was imported. If it is a .zip that is incomplete, take a fresh export on your iPhone and upload it again. If the .zip cannot be opened here and the export XML inside it is under 8 GB, unzip it on a computer and upload that XML instead.
reason_display_messages.collection_interrupted: Your export file ended earlier than expected, so some records are missing. Take a fresh export on your iPhone and upload the new file.
reason_display_messages.records_unreadable: Some entries in your export couldn't be read and were skipped - everything else imported normally. Importing the same file again won't recover them.
reason_display_messages.window_unavailable: Your export doesn't reach back as far as the period asked for, so the dates shown are the dates we actually have.
reason_display_messages.newer_upload_too_large: A newer .zip among your uploads couldn't be opened here, because it is too large or holds too many files, so the export in another of your uploads was imported instead. If you haven't already, unzip that .zip on a computer and, if the export XML inside it is under 8 GB, upload that XML here.
